test_cases.title: Severity-Tagged Logging API Surface Inspection
test_cases.setup: Open libs/log_lib public header and locate the diagnostic logging API declarations.
procedure: Inspect libs/log_lib/include/log_lib/log_api.hpp for the JUNO_LOG_LEVEL_T enum class.
Confirm the enum declares all four severities: JUNO_LOG_LEVEL_DEBUG, JUNO_LOG_LEVEL_INFO, JUNO_LOG_LEVEL_WARN, JUNO_LOG_LEVEL_ERROR.
Confirm the LOG_LIB_API_T vtable declares Log and LogFmt entry points each accepting a JUNO_LOG_LEVEL_T parameter.
Confirm the entry points are part of the public API exported by libs/log_lib.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: log_api.hpp declares JUNO_LOG_LEVEL_T with all four severities and a LOG_LIB_API_T vtable whose Log and LogFmt members accept a JUNO_LOG_LEVEL_T parameter covering every severity.

test_cases.title: Severity Prefix Present on Debug Records
test_cases.setup: Initialize log_lib with a test sink that captures emitted records into a caller-owned buffer.
procedure: Invoke the Log entry point with severity JUNO_LOG_LEVEL_DEBUG and a known message string.
Read the captured record from the test sink buffer.
Assert the captured record begins with the debug severity label.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Captured record starts with the debug severity label prefix before the message body.

test_cases.title: Severity Prefix Distinct Across All Levels
test_cases.setup: Initialize log_lib with a test sink that captures emitted records into a caller-owned buffer.
procedure: Invoke Log with each of the four severities (DEBUG, INFO, WARN, ERROR) and a known message.
Capture each emitted record from the test sink.
Assert each record begins with the severity label corresponding to the severity passed.
Assert the four severity labels are distinct from each other.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Each of the four emitted records carries a distinct severity label prefix matching the JUNO_LOG_LEVEL_T value passed.

test_cases.title: Printf-Style Format String With Variadic Arguments
test_cases.setup: Initialize log_lib with a test sink that captures emitted records into a caller-owned buffer.
procedure: Invoke LogFmt with severity JUNO_LOG_LEVEL_INFO, format string "value=%d name=%s" and arguments (42, "juno").
Capture the emitted record from the test sink.
Assert the record body contains the substring "value=42 name=juno".
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Captured record body includes "value=42 name=juno" demonstrating printf-style substitution of the variadic arguments.

test_cases.title: Format String With Multiple Conversion Specifiers
test_cases.setup: Initialize log_lib with a test sink that captures emitted records into a caller-owned buffer.
procedure: Invoke LogFmt with severity JUNO_LOG_LEVEL_ERROR, format string "%s code=0x%X count=%u" and arguments ("err", 0xDEAD, 7u).
Capture the emitted record from the test sink.
Assert the record body contains the substring "err code=0xDEAD count=7".
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Captured record body contains "err code=0xDEAD count=7" confirming correct handling of multiple conversion specifiers.

test_cases.title: Bounded Output Buffer - Static Allocation Inspection
test_cases.setup: Open libs/log_lib implementation source files (log_common.cpp, log_posix.cpp, log_pico2.cpp).
procedure: Inspect the log_lib implementation for the formatted record output buffer.
Confirm the buffer is a fixed-size stack array of kLogMaxRecord bytes (compile-time constant).
Confirm no calls to malloc, calloc, realloc, new, vasprintf, asprintf, or open_memstream appear in the formatting path.
Confirm the formatting call uses vsnprintf with the fixed buffer length as the bound.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Implementation uses a fixed-size kLogMaxRecord stack buffer and vsnprintf bounded by that length; no heap allocation primitive appears in the diagnostic emission path.

test_cases.title: Oversized Message Truncated Without Overflow
test_cases.setup: Initialize log_lib with a test sink that captures emitted records into a caller-owned buffer larger than the log_lib internal buffer (kLogMaxRecord = 256).
procedure: Construct an input format/message string longer than kLogMaxRecord.
Invoke LogFmt with severity JUNO_LOG_LEVEL_INFO and the oversized payload.
Capture the emitted record length from the test sink.
Assert the captured record length is less than or equal to kLogMaxRecord.
Assert no memory corruption is reported by the test harness (AddressSanitizer clean if enabled).
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Emitted record length does not exceed kLogMaxRecord and the test completes without memory errors.

test_cases.title: Status Code Returned on Successful Emission
test_cases.setup: Initialize log_lib with a test sink configured to accept all writes successfully.
procedure: Invoke Log with each of the four severities (DEBUG, INFO, WARN, ERROR) using a valid message.
Invoke LogFmt with each severity using a valid format string.
Capture the JUNO_STATUS_T return value from each call.
Assert each return value equals JUNO_STATUS_SUCCESS.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: All severity invocations of Log and LogFmt return JUNO_STATUS_SUCCESS when the sink accepts writes.

test_cases.title: Status Code Returned on Sink Failure
test_cases.setup: Initialize log_lib with a test sink configured to fail every write.
procedure: Invoke Log with severity JUNO_LOG_LEVEL_INFO and a valid message.
Capture the JUNO_STATUS_T return value.
Assert the returned status equals JUNO_STATUS_WRITE_ERROR.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Logging call returns JUNO_STATUS_WRITE_ERROR when the underlying sink reports failure.

test_cases.title: Identical Public API on POSIX and Pico2 Builds
test_cases.setup: Open the log_lib public header (log_api.hpp) and the platform implementation files (log_posix.cpp, log_pico2.cpp).
procedure: Inspect log_api.hpp for LOG_LIB_API_T and LOG_LIB_ROOT_T declarations.
Confirm the public header contains no preprocessor branching that changes the visible function signatures by platform.
Locate the LOG_LIB_IMPL_T New() factories in log_posix.cpp and log_pico2.cpp.
Confirm both platform implementations construct a static const LOG_LIB_API_T vtable with identical Log and LogFmt signatures.
Confirm the vtable is constructed exactly once at New() and never reassigned (no global mutable state).
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: log_api.hpp declares one platform-independent API; POSIX and Pico2 implementations both construct an identical-shape LOG_LIB_API_T vtable as a file-scope static const, wired once at New().

test_cases.title: Platform-Specific Sink Selected at Build Time
test_cases.setup: Open libs/log_lib/CMakeLists.txt and the platform-specific implementation source files.
procedure: Inspect libs/log_lib/CMakeLists.txt for platform-conditional source selection (JUNO_FSW_POSIX gate).
Confirm log_posix.cpp compiles into the POSIX build and routes diagnostic output to stderr (file descriptor 2).
Confirm log_pico2.cpp compiles into the Pico2 build and routes diagnostic output to a UART sink, with optional RTT toggle via LOG_LIB_PICO2_USE_RTT.
Confirm sink selection is resolved at configure/compile time, not at runtime.
Confirm the LOG_LIB_IMPL_T instance is file-scope static const (no global mutable state).
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: CMake selects exactly one platform implementation per build; POSIX build emits to stderr and Pico2 build emits to UART (or RTT when LOG_LIB_PICO2_USE_RTT is set), with no runtime sink negotiation.

test_cases.title: No SD or Mission Log Coupling - Code Inspection
test_cases.setup: Open libs/log_lib source tree and CMakeLists.txt.
procedure: Inspect libs/log_lib/CMakeLists.txt for link or include dependencies on mlog_lib, sd_lib, SD card drivers, or filesystem libraries.
Inspect all libs/log_lib source files for include directives referencing mlog_lib, sd_lib, FatFs, or filesystem headers.
Inspect all libs/log_lib source files for symbol references to SD, mlog, or file write APIs.
Confirm none of the above dependencies, includes, or references are present.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: libs/log_lib declares no build dependency on, includes from, or symbol references to mlog_lib, sd_lib, SD card, or filesystem APIs.
